key_insight: HGPTrans predicts vehicle drag directly from surface meshes by combining local graph convolutions, global attention, and hierarchical pooling to capture both fine geometry and long-range aerodynamic interactions.
engineering_relevance: It enables near-real-time drag estimation for early-stage automotive design, dramatically reducing reliance on expensive CFD during large-scale shape exploration.
method: Graph isomorphism convolutions extract discriminative local surface geometry.
Physics-aware slice attention models global, long-range interactions with linear complexity.
Information-redundancy-aware hierarchical pooling compresses the mesh while preserving informative structures.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on DrivAerNet, DrivAerNet++, and a real-vehicle transfer set, the method achieved the best MAE/MSE among baselines and reported relative L1 errors of 1.56% for sedans and 2.12% for SUVs with about 0.293 s inference per vehicle.
watch_item: Performance may depend on mesh quality, pooling ratio, and transfer to unseen vehicle shapes, so robustness outside the tested datasets should be verified.
paper_title: HGPTrans: Hierarchical Graph-Pooling Transolver for Automotive Aerodynamic Drag Coefficient Prediction
